name: dokkan_goku_black
description: Dokkan Battle - Epitome of Sublime Beauty / Goku Black. Clears the stage, taps through the results, handles the intermittent Friend Request popup, then advances to the next level and repeats.

interrupts.name: friend_request
interrupts.note: The Friend Request popup has at least two layouts - a single centred OK ('friend limit reached') and Cancel+OK ('send this user a friend request?'). They share a title, so keying off the title and tapping a fixed offset lands in the gap between the buttons on the two-button layout. Matching the OK button itself and tapping the match centre hits the right button in both, because the match slides onto whichever button is actually there.

steps.name: tap_fight
steps.note: Event stage screen. Template is the word 'Fight' only - it deliberately excludes the ENEMY LV digit, which increments every clear. Entering the event goes blank, then trickles the screen in, then keeps firing effects on the Fight button for seconds afterwards; the template matches partway through that. Measured at the engine's 0.35s poll spacing: the transition runs 13.7-74, the effects afterwards peak at 11.2, and they stop about 3.5s after the transition ends. So wait for motion to drop under 12 - which only the transition exceeds - then hold 3.5s for the effects.

steps.name: tap_start
steps.note: Team select. Team carries over from the previous clear, so no team building is needed. The search window is deliberately generous: events differ in how much sits above this button - Majin Buu's stage screen carries an extra 'Lv. SUPER' banner that Goku Black's does not - and a tight window silently fails to match rather than degrading. The button art is distinctive enough that the wider window costs no accuracy.

steps.name: await_results
steps.note: Battle auto-resolves in this stage - no combat taps, and nothing is tapped while waiting. A Lv.11 battle took 66s where the Lv.3 in the source recording was instant, so this just waits it out.

steps.name: tap_results_ok
steps.note: OK only becomes tappable once the reward reveal finishes. The nudge taps an inert part of the results panel to skip that animation - it belongs here, not on await_results, where it would be tapping into a live battle.

steps.name: tap_next_level
steps.note: 'GO TO THE NEXT LEVEL' is a tap-anywhere screen; tapping dead centre avoids every button. The text fades in over about a second and the loading before it varies, so the gate matches well before the screen accepts input. Rather than guess a fixed delay, wait for the frame to stop changing, then hold 1.5s. Measured on the source recording: while loading or fading the frame-to-frame difference is 5.9-33, once settled it is under 1.5, so 3.0 sits in a wide gap. This needs no template for the loading screen, which is the thing nothing recognises.
